props.name: product
props.type: atlas | austeris | dowel | efema | furca | hilvan | kasl | kasl-server | kilna | lacodda | lyrid | lyrn | midda | nitid | nooma | rhapsod | rigger | scheda | sefy | turnout
props.description: Which product's mark to draw.

props.name: name
props.description: The product's name, as it is written.

props.name: version
props.description: The version, as the product shows it: "v0.31.0".

props.name: tagline
props.description: The one-line promise, as on the product's README.

props.name: children
props.description: What the product adds: licence, links, where its data lives.

props.name: lineLabel
props.description: The words beside λ, e.g. "Part of the lacodda line".

props.name: lineHref
props.description: Where those words lead, if anywhere.

props.name: level
props.description: Where the product's name stands in the page's outline: `2` by default, under the title of the screen or dialog the plate sits in.

components.name: Accordion
components.description: Groups the items and decides how many can be open. `single` (the default, `multiple={false}`) closes the others when one opens; `multiple` lets any number stay open together. Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or left to manage itself with `defaultValue`.

components.name: AccordionItem
components.description: One section: a header with its trigger, and the panel it opens.

components.name: AccordionHeader
components.description: The heading a reader moving by heading lands on, open or shut. The trigger lives inside it, never beside it - a section title that exists only as a button's accessible name is not a heading a reader can navigate to.

props.name: level
props.description: Where the sections stand in the page's outline: `3` by default, under a screen's title and a section's. A page that opens straight onto the accordion says `2`.

components.name: AccordionTrigger
components.description: The button that opens and shuts its section's panel. The chevron rotates with `data-panel-open`, the same attribute a reader's `aria-expanded` follows, so the two can never disagree.

components.name: AccordionPanel
components.description: The section's content. Animates by its own measured height through `--accordion-panel-height`, exactly as `CollapsiblePanel` does - the same reasoning applies unchanged: a fixed max-height guess is either too small for long content or a visible pause for short content, and the measured variable is neither.

components.name: ActionBar
components.description: The bar.

components.name: ActionBarButton
components.description: A button in the bar. Give it the set's own `Button` through `render`, so the toolbar's arrow keys reach it and the button keeps its variants.

components.name: ActionBarSeparator
components.description: A rule between groups of actions. Decorative, and announced as a separator rather than as a control.

components.name: ActionBarGroup
components.description: A group of related actions inside the bar - the three alignment buttons, a pair of toggles. Groups the arrows walk as one.

components.name: ActionBarSpacer
components.description: Pushes what follows to the far end. A plain spacer, so a bar can put Cancel beside Save and everything else to the left without a wrapper.

props.name: entries
props.description: What is known about each date. Dates with no entry are drawn as nothing recorded, which is a different fact from a value of zero.

props.name: from
props.description: First date of the range, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

props.name: to
props.description: Last date.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: The day a week starts on, Sunday-first like `Date#getUTCDay`. Monday by default. It decides which row a date lands on, so it is stated rather than guessed from a locale this cannot see.

props.name: busiest
props.description: The ceiling the shades are measured against. Defaults to the largest value present; state it to compare two grids by eye.

props.name: label
props.description: What the grid as a whole is, for a reader who cannot see it.

props.name: describe
props.description: What one square says. Given the cell, returns the sentence that becomes its hover title and its accessible name - the caller owns it because only the caller knows whether a value is hours, words or commits.

props.name: weekdayLabel
props.description: Row labels, one per weekday in drawing order. Omitted entirely rather than defaulted: a weekday name is a word in a language this cannot pick.

props.name: less
props.description: The word at the faint end - "less", usually.

props.name: more
props.description: The word at the dark end.

props.name: busiest
props.description: What the darkest square stands for, in words: the scale is relative, and without this the shades read as an absolute measure. Omitted when there is no value in the grid to be busiest.

props.name: none
props.description: The empty square: no entry for that date. Omitted by a caller whose data cannot produce that kind.

props.name: partial
props.description: The outlined square: under way, no total yet. Omitted by a caller whose data cannot produce that kind.

props.name: icon
props.description: Drawn before the text. The product's own, because an icon that means "warning" here should be the one it means everywhere else in the product.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading. Optional: a one-line alert does not need one.

props.name: action
props.description: Anything that goes at the end - a link to the thing that fixes it, a dismiss button the product owns.

components.name: AppShell
components.description: The frame.

props.name: top
props.description: The strip across the top, full width - a title bar, a header, a banner row. Leave it out and the rail runs to the top of the window.

props.name: side
props.description: The rail down the left. Leave it out for a product that navigates from the top bar alone, which is the usual shape on the web.

props.name: sideWidth
props.description: How wide the rail is. A number is pixels; a string is any CSS track size, for a rail that collapses or is dragged. Defaults to the theme's `--spacing-rail`, so four products stop each choosing their own.

props.name: topHeight
props.description: How tall the top bar is, same rules, defaulting to `--spacing-titlebar`. It is a fixed track rather than `auto` on purpose: a bar that grows by a pixel when its content changes moves every screen under it.

components.name: Screen
components.description: One screen inside the frame, handed the height the window has left.

props.name: name
props.description: Who or what this stands for. Always required: it is the name a reader who does not see the picture gets, and the source of the initials.

props.name: src
props.description: The picture. Absent, or failing to load, falls back to the initials.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Anything to draw instead of the initials when there is no picture - an icon for a thing that is not a person.

props.name: imgProps
props.description: Passed to the ``, for `loading` or `referrerPolicy`.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.description: A row of faces, overlapping, with a count for the rest.

props.name: max
props.description: How many tiles to show before the rest become a count.

props.name: people
props.description: The people. Given as data rather than as children, because the group has to know how many there are to say how many are hidden.

props.name: size
props.type: sm | md | xs | lg | xl | null
props.description: The size of every tile in the row, the count included.

props.name: label
props.description: What the whole row is called, for a screen reader - "Assignees", in the product's word.

props.name: variant
props.type: outline | soft | accent | good | warn | bad | info

props.name: tone
props.type: neutral | accent | good | warn | bad | info

props.name: sticky
props.description: Pinned to the top of the viewport, above the application's own chrome. For the ones that must not scroll away - offline, expired.

props.name: icon
props.description: Drawn first. The product's own icon, for the same reason as Alert's.

props.name: action
props.description: Anything at the end: a button that fixes it, a link, a dismiss the product decides is allowed.

props.name: bars
props.description: One column per entry, in order. A `null` value keeps its place and is drawn as a gap.

props.name: max
props.description: The top of the scale. Defaults to the tallest bar present; state it to compare two charts, or to hold a scale still while the data moves.

props.name: label
props.description: What the whole chart is, in words.

props.name: value
props.description: Where it sits, on the same scale as the bars.

props.name: max
props.description: The same ceiling the chart is drawn against.

props.name: children
props.description: What the line is, beside it.

props.name: gutter
props.description: Room on the right for the baseline's label. Omit it where there is no baseline, or where the label is short enough to live in the panel's own padding.

components.name: BigCalendarDayContext
components.description: Whether a line stands in the day the month's keyboard is on: `true` there, `false` in every other day, `null` outside a month.

props.name: color
props.description: The item's own colour - any CSS colour, `var(--series-3)` for a category. Neutral without one.

props.name: tentative
props.description: A plan rather than a booking: a dashed outline.

props.name: done
props.description: It has happened: drawn quieter, still pressable.

props.name: start
props.description: Before the words - a cover, a dot.

props.name: end
props.description: After the words - the glyphs that mark it: a kind, a lock, a status. They do not shrink; the words truncate.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to draw: the product's link, a hover card's trigger. Without it the item is a `<button>` when it has `onClick`, and a `<div>` when it has nothing to do.

props.name: onAddDay
props.description: Add something on this day: a plus in the corner of the day under the pointer, and the first stop of Tab from the day the cursor is on.

props.name: addDayLabel
props.description: Names the plus. Required with it: an icon with no name announces nothing.

props.name: month
props.description: Any day of the month to show.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.description: Asked for when the keyboard walks off the grid; any day of the new month. Without it the cursor stops at the edge.

props.name: renderDay
props.description: What a day holds, one node per line, each with a `key`.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: The words of the count a full day folds into, given how many are folded: "3 more".

props.name: fewerLabel
props.description: The words that fold an open day again.

props.name: onDaySelect
props.description: Pressing a day - a click on its ground, or Enter on the cursor.

props.name: dropTarget
props.description: The day something being carried would land on.

props.name: dropHint
props.description: What landing on `dropTarget` would mean, said at the foot of it.

props.name: locale
props.description: Names the months and the weekdays, and picks the first day of the week: `en-GB` starts on Monday, `en-US` on Sunday, `en-u-fw-mon` on Monday whatever the region. The application's language by default.

props.name: label
props.description: What the trail is called for a reader - "Breadcrumb" by convention, but a product with two of them on one screen should say which.

props.name: items
props.description: The trail, root first. The last item is where the reader stands.

props.name: render
props.description: The element a crumb before the last is drawn as. Without it a crumb is a button and `onSelect` says which was pressed.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the id of a crumb before the last when it is pressed, whatever element it is drawn as.

props.name: max
props.description: How many crumbs are drawn before the middle is folded away. The first and the last are always kept, so this is a floor of three.

props.name: variant
props.type: primary | ghost | soft | danger | icon | link

props.name: size
props.type: xs | sm | md | icon-xs | icon-sm | icon-md

props.name: disabledReason
props.description: Why the button cannot be pressed, in the product's words - read only while `disabled`.

props.name: render
props.description: Render something else with the button's clothes on - a link, most often.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected day, or `undefined` for none.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the day the reader chose. It fires on Enter and on a click, not on the arrows - those only move the cursor.

props.name: month
props.description: Which month is shown. Uncontrolled unless given.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.description: Called with the new month when the shown month changes: the paging buttons, or the cursor arrowing off the end of a month.

props.name: min
props.description: Bounds, inclusive. A day outside them cannot be chosen.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest day that can be chosen, inclusive. See `min`.

props.name: rangeEnd
props.description: For a range: the other end, so the days between can be shaded.

props.name: locale
props.description: Formats the names. The application's language by default - see `useLocale`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: What the grid is called, for a screen reader.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Put the focus on the day under the cursor when it mounts - for a calendar that opens in a popup, where choosing a day is what the reader came for. Left to the popup, the focus went to the first thing in it: the month-paging button, two Tabs away from the days.

props.name: previousMonthLabel
props.description: Names the buttons that page the months. Required: they are icons, and an icon with no name is a button that announces nothing.

props.name: nextMonthLabel
props.description: Names the button that pages to the next month. Required, for the same reason as `previousMonthLabel`.

props.name: children
props.description: The words next to the box. Omit only for a checkbox in a table cell, and then give `aria-label` instead.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled state. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state when the checkbox is uncontrolled.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the box is toggled.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Some but not all of what this stands for is checked. Draws a dash; clicking still checks everything.

props.name: parent
props.description: This is the box that stands for the whole group. Inside a `CheckboxGroup` with `allValues`, its state follows the children - checked, unchecked, or the dash in between - and clicking it sets all of them. Working that out by hand is where the indeterminate state usually goes wrong, so the group does it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops the box taking input; the label dims with it.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the box as required for form validation.

props.name: name
props.description: The field name submitted with a form.

props.name: value
props.description: What this box contributes to the group's `value` array when checked, and what a form submits for it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name, for a checkbox with no `children`.

props.name: value
props.description: The values of the checked boxes. Controlled; pair it with `onValueChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The values checked at first, when the group is uncontrolled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new list of checked values.

props.name: allValues
props.description: Every value in the group, which is what makes a parent checkbox work.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every box in the group.

props.name: variant
props.type: outline | dashed | soft | accent | good | warn | bad | info

props.name: count
props.description: Shown after the label, for a count.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Called when the cross is pressed. Giving it is what makes the chip removable; the press does not reach a clickable parent.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the cross, for example "Remove tag". Required with `onRemove`, and there is no default word, so the product can translate it.

props.name: pressed
props.description: Whether it is on. Controlled; pair it with `onPressedChange`.

props.name: defaultPressed
props.description: Whether it starts on, for a chip nobody else needs to know about.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the chip is switched. Giving it makes the chip a switch.

props.name: value
props.description: Which member of a ChipGroup this is. Inside a group the group owns the state, and `pressed` is not read.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops the chip being switched, and dims it. Only a switch can be disabled.

components.name: ChipGroup
components.description: A row of chips that switch together.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: What the row of chips is: "Kind", "Status". A group without a name is a row of buttons a reader meets one at a time with no idea what they choose between.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: value
props.description: The values of the chips that are on. An array in both modes, because that is Base UI's shape and a single mode is a group that holds at most one.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The values that start on, when the group keeps its own state.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the values that are on after a chip is pressed. Always an array, in both modes.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several on at once - filters - rather than one at a time - a kind.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every chip in the group.

props.name: code
props.description: The code, as it should land on the clipboard. Always required, even when `tokens` is given: what is copied is the text, not a reassembly of the highlighting.

props.name: tokens
props.description: The same code, coloured. Lines of tokens - one array per line, and the newlines are the array boundaries rather than characters in the text. Left out, the block draws `code` in one colour.

props.name: caption
props.description: Shown above the code: a file name, a path, a language. It is what brings the header; without one the copy button floats over the code instead, because a strip holding nothing but a button that hides until hover is empty furniture.

props.name: numbered
props.description: Numbers down the left. Off by default: they are for code a reader is meant to refer to, and on a two-line command they are furniture.

props.name: firstLine
props.description: Where the numbering starts, for an excerpt lifted out of a file.

props.name: highlight
props.description: Lines to mark, in the same numbering the reader sees.

props.name: copyLabel
props.description: Brings the copy button, and names it for a screen reader. Required to have one, and deliberately without a default: a string this component invents is a string the product cannot translate.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.description: Announced after a successful copy. Required alongside `copyLabel`.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Told what happened, for a product that wants its own toast.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let long lines wrap instead of scrolling.

components.name: Collapsible
components.description: Groups the trigger and the panel. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or left to manage itself with `defaultOpen`.

components.name: CollapsibleTrigger
components.description: The button that opens and shuts the panel. The chevron rotates with `data-panel-open`, the same attribute a reader's `aria-expanded` follows, so the two can never say different things.

components.name: CollapsiblePanel
components.description: The region that opens and shuts. Animates by its own measured height through `--collapsible-panel-height`, so content of any length - one line or a page of it - opens by its real size rather than a guessed maximum.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen colour: a token name, or a hex string.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Told the next colour: a token name from the palette, or a hex string once the free box holds a complete one.

props.name: allowCustom
props.description: Whether the reader may type a colour of their own.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the palette for a screen reader.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the element that names the palette, when a visible label does it.

props.name: swatchLabel
props.description: How a swatch is named. Takes the colour's name, so the product can say "Lime" in its own language rather than shipping ours.

props.name: customLabel
props.description: The label on the free-entry box, when `allowCustom` is on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the field and stops it taking input: every swatch and the free box.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the column for assistive technology: "Resize the Tier column".

props.name: hint
props.description: Shown on hover: how to drag and how to reset.

props.name: onResize
props.description: The width while dragging, and once more with `done` when the pointer is let go - the moment to persist.

props.name: onReset
props.description: Double-click: the column goes back to its natural width.

props.name: onStart
props.description: Called on pointerdown, before the first `onResize` - the moment for the caller to measure what every column is before the layout goes fixed.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Narrower than this and the column is a stripe with nothing in it.

components.name: Combobox
components.description: The root. `items` is what gets filtered; `multiple` turns the value into an array and makes the chips meaningful.

components.name: ComboboxInputGroup
components.description: The wrapper for an input with something beside it - a clear button, an icon, the chips.

components.name: ComboboxTrigger
components.description: The button that opens the list without typing, for a reader who wants to see everything there is.

components.name: ComboboxIcon
components.description: The chevron. Decorative.

components.name: ComboboxGroup
components.description: A labelled group of rows.

components.name: ComboboxCollection
components.description: The rows of one group, as a render function over that group's items.

components.name: ComboboxItemIndicator
components.description: The tick, drawn only on a chosen row.

components.name: ComboboxStatus
components.description: A polite live region for the state of an asynchronous list. Stays mounted, like `Empty`, so the announcement actually fires.

components.name: ComboboxChips
components.description: The container the chips sit in. Its children are plain nodes, not a render function - the chosen values are mapped by `ComboboxValue` inside it.

props.name: ref
props.description: Allows getting a ref to the component instance. Once the component unmounts, React will set `ref.current` to `null` (or call the ref with `null` if you passed a callback ref).

components.name: ComboboxValue
components.description: The current value, as a render function of it. This is what turns a `multiple` value into one chip per entry.

components.name: ComboboxInput
components.description: Where the query is typed. A real `<input role="combobox">`.

components.name: ComboboxClear
components.description: Empties the value. Base UI hides it while there is nothing to clear.

components.name: ComboboxPopup
components.description: The list. Portalled and positioned against the input, or the given anchor.

props.name: side
props.type: bottom | top | left | right | inline-end | inline-start
props.description: Preferred side of the input. Base UI flips it when it does not fit.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment along that side.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Distance from the input, in pixels.

props.name: anchor
props.type: Element | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null) | null
props.description: What to line the list up with. Defaults to the input that owns it.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the raised host of the overlay this is opened inside (`layer.tsx`), and to the document body when there is none - either way not the element it was opened from, whose `overflow` would clip it. Pass an element to put it somewhere else, such as a container being screenshotted.

components.name: ComboboxList
components.description: The rows, as a list. Undressed: it is a wrapper, and the popup around it already carries the border and the padding.

components.name: ComboboxItem
components.description: A row.

components.name: ComboboxEmpty
components.description: What is shown when nothing matched. The words are the product's.

components.name: ComboboxChip
components.description: One chosen value, in a multiple combobox. Focusable, so it can be reached and removed without a pointer.

components.name: ComboboxChipRemove
components.description: The X on a chip. A real button, which is what makes Backspace and Enter both work on it.

components.name: ComboboxGroupLabel
components.description: The caption above a group.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description: The root. Controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange`, because what opens a palette is a shortcut somewhere else in the application.

components.name: CommandPaletteItem
components.description: A row. The same clothes as a Combobox row, on purpose: a palette is a list of choices, and two lists of choices in one product should not differ.

components.name: CommandPaletteList
components.description: The list. Takes a render function over the filtered items.

components.name: CommandPaletteEmpty
components.description: Shown when nothing matches. The words are the product's.

components.name: CommandPaletteGroup
components.description: A labelled group, for a palette that lists more than one kind of thing.

components.name: CommandPaletteGroupLabel
components.description: The caption above a group.

components.name: CommandPaletteCollection
components.description: The rows of one group, as a render function over that group's items.

components.name: CommandPalettePopup
components.description: The palette itself: a dim over the page, and the box in the upper third of it - where the eye already is, rather than dead centre.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: What the palette is called, for a screen reader. Required, and required for a reason particular to this component: the popup is a dialog, and a dialog is named by its own visible title - which a palette does not have, because the field is the first thing in it.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the document body.

components.name: CommandPaletteInput
components.description: The field. Sits inside the popup, which is what makes the popup a dialog and the field its combobox.

props.name: hint
props.description: Shown at the right of the field, as `Escape`. Decorative.

components.name: CommandPaletteRow
components.description: The row's own layout: an icon, what it is, and where it lives.

props.name: icon
props.description: Drawn before the label. Size and colour are the product's.

props.name: hint
props.description: Drawn after the label, small and faint - where the item lives, such as a section name or a shortcut.

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.description: The root. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or left to manage itself around a `ConfirmDialogTrigger`.

components.name: ConfirmDialogTrigger
components.description: What opens it. Give it `render` to use your own button.

components.name: ConfirmDialogClose
components.description: What closes it - and the only thing that does, which is why a confirm dialog with no `ConfirmDialogClose` inside it is a trap.

components.name: ConfirmDialogBackdrop
components.description: The scrim. Darker than the Dialog's, because what is behind it is not just out of reach for a moment - it is waiting on an answer.

components.name: ConfirmDialogPopup
components.description: The dialog itself, announced as `alertdialog`. Portalled, so it is not clipped by whatever it was opened from.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the document body, which is what keeps the popup from being clipped by an ancestor. Pass an element to put it somewhere else - inside an overlay that is already open, or into a container being screenshotted.

props.name: backdrop
props.description: Whether to draw the scrim. On by default, and it should stay on for anything a person actually uses: the dim is what says the page behind is out of reach. Turn it off where the popup is shown alongside other things on purpose - a component gallery, a screenshot - because a scrim is `position: fixed` and covers everything, not only its own container.

components.name: ConfirmDialogTitle
components.description: The question. Base UI points the popup's `aria-labelledby` at it, so this is what a screen reader reads out when the dialog interrupts.

components.name: ConfirmDialogDescription
components.description: What the answer costs, and the popup's `aria-describedby`. On this dialog it is close to required: the title asks, the description says what happens.

components.name: ConfirmDialogHeader
components.description: The top: the question and what it costs. The dialog's part, under this one's name.

components.name: ConfirmDialogBody
components.description: The part that scrolls, for consequences too long to fit. The dialog's part, under this one's name.

components.name: ConfirmDialogActions
components.description: Where the two answers go, pinned to the bottom and right-aligned, because the choice belongs where the eye leaves the sentence. The dialog's part, under this one's name.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.description: The root. It positions against the pointer, so there is nothing to anchor and nothing to control but `onOpenChange`.

components.name: ContextMenuTrigger
components.description: The area that opens it. A `<div>`, not a button: give it `render` to make it the row or the canvas it belongs to rather than a wrapper.

components.name: ContextMenuGroup

components.name: Dialog
components.description: The root. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or left to manage itself around a `Dialog.Trigger`.

components.name: DialogTrigger
components.description: What opens it. Give it `render` to use your own button.

components.name: DialogClose
components.description: What closes it - the same, for a cancel button or an X.

components.name: DialogBackdrop
components.description: The scrim. Dark because a modal is a modal: what is behind it is out of reach, and saying so with contrast is the only thing that reads at a glance.

components.name: DialogPopup
components.description: The dialog itself. Portalled, so it is not clipped by whatever it was opened from. Put a `DialogHeader`, a `DialogBody` and `DialogActions` inside it.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the document body, which is what keeps the popup from being clipped by whatever it was opened from. Pass an element to put it somewhere else - inside a dialog that is already open, or into a container being screenshotted.

props.name: backdrop
props.description: Whether to draw the scrim. On by default, and it should stay on for anything a person actually uses: the dim is what says the page behind is out of reach. Turn it off where the popup is shown alongside other things on purpose - a component gallery, a screenshot - because a scrim is `position: fixed` and covers everything, not only its own container.

components.name: DialogHeader
components.description: The top of the popup: the title, the line under it, and an action beside them. It stays put while the body scrolls.

props.name: action
props.description: Beside the title, at the end of the line: a close button, a menu. The title and description wrap under themselves rather than under it.

components.name: DialogBody
components.description: The part that scrolls. It takes the height the header and the actions leave, and only it moves when there is more than fits. It takes a ref, for a dialog that opens with the focus on what it says rather than on a button.

components.name: DialogActions
components.description: Where the actions go, pinned to the bottom. Right-aligned, because the primary action of a dialog belongs where the eye leaves the sentence.

props.name: start
props.description: At the other end of the row from the answer: the action that is not the answer to the dialog's question - "Delete" on an editor whose question is "Save?". Kept apart so it is not pressed on the way to "Save".

components.name: DialogTitle
components.description: The heading. Base UI points the popup's `aria-labelledby` at it, so a dialog with one is named for a screen reader without anyone arranging it.

components.name: DialogDescription
components.description: The line under the heading, and the popup's `aria-describedby`.

props.name: before
props.description: The text as it was, drawn on the left.

props.name: after
props.description: The text as it is now, drawn on the right.

props.name: beforeLabel
props.description: What each side is called - a version name, a date, "on disk".

props.name: afterLabel
props.description: What the right side is called; see `beforeLabel`.

props.name: summary
props.description: The line above the comparison: how much moved. The component counts, the product says it in words - a count is a plural, and a plural belongs to a language the component does not know. Given the two numbers, and left out entirely when there is nothing to say.

props.name: numbered
props.description: Numbers down each side. On by default: a comparison is usually read in order to go and change something, and the number is how the reader finds the place.

props.name: copyLabel
props.description: Brings a copy button to each side's header, and names it.

props.name: copiedLabel
props.description: Announced after a successful copy. Required alongside `copyLabel`.

props.name: onCopy
props.description: Told what happened, for a product that wants its own toast.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Declared here rather than taken from the variants: cva types a variant as nullable, and `aria-orientation` is not - a `null` passed through would be a type error at the call site and an attribute React drops.

props.name: label
props.description: A caption sitting in the line: "Today", "Archived", "or". Horizontal only - there is no reading direction that puts a word inside a vertical rule.

props.name: decorative
props.description: A rule that is styling rather than structure. Taken out of the accessibility tree, so a reader is not told about it.

components.name: SectionHeader
components.description: The heading over a part of a screen, with what belongs to that part at the far end of the same row.

props.name: title
props.description: The section's heading, drawn at `level`.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the title, saying what the section holds.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons belonging to this section rather than to the screen - Add, Collapse, a link out.

props.name: level
props.description: Where the section stands in the outline: `2` by default.

components.name: Drawer
components.description: The root. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or left to manage itself around a `DrawerTrigger`.

components.name: DrawerTrigger
components.description: What opens it. Give it `render` to use your own button.

components.name: DrawerClose
components.description: What closes it - the same, for a cancel button or an X.

components.name: DrawerBackdrop
components.description: The scrim. Dark because a drawer is modal: what is behind it is out of reach, and saying so with contrast is the only thing that reads at a glance.

components.name: DrawerPopup
components.description: The panel. Portalled, and wrapped in its own viewport so the edge it is pinned to holds still while the body scrolls. Put a `DrawerHeader`, a `DrawerBody` and `DrawerActions` inside it.

props.name: container

props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the document body, which is what keeps the popup from being clipped by an ancestor. Pass an element to put it somewhere else - inside an overlay that is already open, or into a container being screenshotted.

props.name: backdrop
props.description: Whether to draw the scrim. On by default, and it should stay on for anything a person actually uses: the dim is what says the page behind is out of reach. Turn it off where the popup is shown alongside other things on purpose - a component gallery, a screenshot - because a scrim is `position: fixed` and covers everything, not only its own container.

components.name: DrawerTitle
components.description: The heading. Base UI points the popup's `aria-labelledby` at it, so a drawer with one is named for a screen reader without anyone arranging it.

components.name: DrawerDescription
components.description: The line under the heading, and the popup's `aria-describedby`.

components.name: DrawerHeader
components.description: The top of the panel: the title, the line under it, and an action beside them. The dialog's part, under the drawer's name.

components.name: DrawerBody
components.description: The part that scrolls. The dialog's part, under the drawer's name.

components.name: DrawerActions
components.description: Where the actions go, pinned to the bottom edge of the panel however little is in it - a drawer is tall, and its buttons should not wander up the page. The dialog's part, under the drawer's name.

props.name: value
props.description: Minutes, or `null` for empty.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Told the new minutes (or `null` when emptied) on blur and on Enter, not on every key, and only when the parsed value differs from `value`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: What a reader sees before they type. A duration in the canonical spelling is the best hint there is, so this is the product's to give.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops the field taking input.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows the value but does not let it be edited.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field as required for form validation.

props.name: name
props.description: The field name submitted with a form.

props.name: id
props.description: Put on the input, so a label can point at it.

props.name: ref
props.description: A ref to the underlying `<input>`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name, when there is no visible label.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Points at the hint or error text for the field.

components.name: EmptyMark
components.description: The line's hexagon, at whatever size the caller asks for.

components.name: FilteredMark
components.description: The same hexagon, cut by a slash. For a filter that matched nothing: the shape is there, the contents are not.

components.name: ErrorMark
components.description: A hexagon with a corner broken out of it. For something that failed.

props.name: title
props.description: What is not here, in the product's words.

props.name: body
props.description: Why, or what to do about it.

props.name: action
props.description: The one thing worth doing here. An empty screen with no way out is a dead end.

props.name: mark
props.description: Something other than the default mark - a product's own illustration. A plain empty state draws no mark, its own or the default.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Draw something else instead of the default screen.

props.name: resetKey
props.description: Change this to clear the error - a route, usually.

props.name: onError
props.description: Somewhere to send it. The product owns whether that is a log, a file or a service - the boundary only knows it happened.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words on the default screen. Required, and not defaulted: they are the only text here, and English inside a primitive is text no product can translate.

props.name: label
props.description: What the control is called. Always rendered; `labelHidden` only takes it off the screen.

props.name: children
props.description: The control itself - Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, anything.

props.name: help

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong, if anything. Its presence is what marks the control invalid - there is no separate `invalid` prop to keep in step.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Keep the label for screen readers but take it off the screen. For a field whose meaning is obvious in context - a search box in a toolbar.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field required, which is a statement about the form rather than about validation: the label gets the mark a reader looks for.

props.name: name
props.description: The control's `name`, forwarded so a `Form` can attach a server error to this field by name.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control, and dims a `beside` control's label with it.

props.name: beside
props.description: The control beside its name, inside the label, rather than under a caption: for a Switch or a Checkbox.

components.name: FieldGroup
components.description: FieldGroup - one name for several controls.

props.name: label
props.description: What the group is called - "Type", "References". Always rendered; `labelHidden` only takes it off the screen.

props.name: children
props.description: The controls: a row of chips, a segment, a grid of pictures, several checkboxes. Anything - a group names its contents rather than handing them an id.

props.description: A hint under the group, read as the group's description. Hidden while an error is showing, as in Field.

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong with the group as a whole - "choose at least one".

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Keep the legend for screen readers but take it off the screen.

props.name: required
props.description: Adds the mark a reader looks for to the legend. A statement about the form; the group does not validate anything itself.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every native control inside, which is what a `<fieldset>` does on its own.

props.name: onFiles
props.description: Called with the files that passed the filters.

props.name: onReject
props.description: Called with the ones that did not, so the product can say why.

props.name: accept
props.description: What to take, in the form `<input accept>` uses: `image/*`, `.pdf,.docx`.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Largest file, in bytes.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: How many at once. Without it, any number.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether several may be chosen in the picker.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the zone, ignores drops and disables the input underneath.

props.name: children
props.description: What the zone says. The product's words, in the product's language.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the field for a screen reader, when there is no visible label.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The `id` of the element that names the field, when it is not the zone's own text.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The `id` of the element that describes the field - the accepted types, the size limit.

props.name: label
props.description: What the funnel says to assistive technology and on hover.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: The words of the button inside the panel that empties the filter.

props.name: children
props.description: The controls: a text box, checkboxes, whatever narrows this column.

props.name: className
props.description: On the trigger, for showing it on hover or always.

props.name: align
props.description: Which edge of the funnel the panel lines up with. Defaults to `start`.

props.name: foot
props.description: What stands under it: a composer, a status line.

components.name: Pane
components.description: A panel whose bars stand and whose body scrolls between them.

props.name: label
props.description: What the body holds: the scroll region's name, which it needs because it becomes a tab stop when it overflows - "Works", "Version 3".

props.name: head
props.description: The bar across the top: a title and what acts on the open thing.

props.name: foot
props.description: The bar across the foot: a status, tags, a button that adds a row.

props.name: bodyClassName
props.description: The body's padding. A list's rows pad themselves; prose needs room.

props.name: viewportRef
props.description: The scrolling element, for a caller that reads or sets the position.

components.name: ListDetail

props.name: list
props.description: The list, usually a `Pane` of `RowButton`s.

props.name: detail
props.description: What is open in it, or what says nothing is.

props.name: width

props.name: side
props.description: Which side the list stands on. A queue read against a month stands after it.

components.name: ListDetailBack
components.description: The way back to the list, for the width at which the list is not on screen. Drawn only there: beside the list it would be a button that returns to where the reader already is.

props.name: label
props.description: What it says: "All works", "Settings". The product's word, shown beside the arrow.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Called when the button is pressed. The screen uses it to close the open thing and show the list again.

components.description: A box that keeps its shape before, during and after whatever fills it loads. `size-full` on the child is the contract: this component reserves the rectangle, the child covers it.

props.name: ratio
props.description: The box's shape: `square`, `video`, or a raw number as width / height - `4 / 3`, `21 / 9` - for anything the named steps do not cover.

props.name: fit
props.description: How the picture fills a box that is not its own shape. `cover` for a photo standing in for the whole box; `contain` for a logo or a diagram where cropping would cut off the point of it.

props.description: Required, with no default: a decorative picture says so explicitly with `alt=""` rather than by omission, which is indistinguishable from a picture nobody described yet.

props.name: fallback
props.description: What stands in the box when the picture fails to load - the product's text or icon, not a default this component would have to write in some one language.

props.description: What the value is called: the caption above it.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Keep the caption for a screen reader and take it off the screen - for a cell whose column header already names it.

props.description: What an empty value shows. A dash reads as "nothing yet"; a blank box reads as a rendering fault.

props.description: Shows the value and refuses to edit it.

props.description: The stored value; `null` for none.

props.name: onCommit
props.description: Called once, with the parsed value, when a change is kept. Return `false` to refuse it - a server that said no - and the field goes back to the stored value.

props.name: codec
props.description: How the value is read from the text and spelled back. Left out, the value is plain text.

props.name: ref
props.description: React 19 passes `ref` as a plain prop; it is declared so callers can reach the element to focus it or read its selection.

props.name: value
props.description: The document to show: anything `JSON.parse` returns.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new set of open paths whenever a branch is opened or closed. Pair it with `open` to control the viewer.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Told which row was activated, with its path and its value. What a product hangs "copy this" or "go to this setting" on.

props.name: label
props.description: What a screen reader calls it. Required, and without a default: a string this component invents is a string the product cannot translate.

props.name: root
props.description: The path the document starts at, for a viewer showing one field of a larger record. Paths are then written so they still mean something in that record.

props.name: keys
props.description: A shortcut in the line's notation - `Mod+K`, `G D`, `?`. Given this, the component draws each key under this platform's own name. Without it, the children are the key.

components.name: KeyValueRow

props.name: label
props.description: The name of the fact.

props.name: children
props.description: What it is. A node rather than a string: half the values in a real panel are a Badge, a RelativeTime or a link.

props.name: className
props.description: Dresses the pair as a whole when the layout is `stacked`, and the term alone in `rows`.

components.name: LayerProvider

props.name: above
props.type: menu | popup | floating | overlay | modal | palette
props.description: The rung the overlay itself stands on: `modal` for a dialog or a drawer, `palette` for the command palette, `floating` for a popover, `overlay` for a product's own full-screen stage.

props.name: mount
props.description: Where the layer goes: the overlay's own portal node. Every overlay of the set passes it, and it matters for the modal ones. A modal dialog hides everything outside its portal from assistive technology - Base UI marks the rest of the body `aria-hidden` - and a layer beside the portal rather than in it was hidden with the page: the menu opened in a drawer worked for a pointer and did not exist for a screen reader. Inside the portal the layer counts as the overlay's own. Without it the layer goes into the layer it was opened in, or onto the body.

props.name: points
props.description: The readings, in order. `value: null` is a measurement not taken.

props.name: bounds
props.description: Override any edge of the plot. `min: 0` for a count, where zero is the truth rather than a flattening.

props.name: label
props.description: What the chart as a whole says, for a reader who cannot see it.

props.name: ticks

props.name: formatTick
props.description: Turns a tick into its label. Without it the number is drawn as it is - which is right for a count and wrong for money or a duration.

props.name: footer
props.description: The labels under the axis - usually the first and last reading. Two or three, not one per point: the axis is not a place for a list.

components.name: ListRow

props.name: start
props.description: What identifies the row at a glance: an icon, a status dot, a cover.

props.name: description
props.description: A second line under the words, quieter and truncated the same way.

props.name: end
props.description: What is measured about the row: a date, a count, a chip.

props.name: children
props.description: The row's words.

props.name: render
props.description: Something other than a `div` - an `<li>` in a `<ul>`, most often: `render={<li />}`.

components.name: RowButton
components.description: A row that is a choice.

props.name: start
props.description: What identifies the row at a glance: an icon, a status dot, a cover.

props.name: description
props.description: A second line under the words, quieter and truncated the same way.

props.name: end
props.description: What is measured about the row: a date, a count, a chip.

props.name: children
props.description: The row's words.

props.name: selected
