props.type: bottom | top | left | right | inline-end | inline-start
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger. Base UI flips it when it does not fit.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment along that side.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Distance from the trigger, in pixels.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the raised host of the overlay this is opened inside (`layer.tsx`), and to the document body when there is none - either way not the element it was opened from, whose `overflow` would clip it. Pass an element to put it somewhere else, such as a container being screenshotted.

components.name: SelectItem
components.description: An option, with the tick that says it is the chosen one.

props.name: indicator
props.description: Draw the tick on the chosen item. Pass `false` for a list where the choice is obvious some other way.

components.name: SelectGroupLabel
components.description: The caption above a group.

components.name: SelectSeparator
components.description: A line between groups of options.

components.name: ShortcutList
components.description: The list on its own, for a settings page that shows the keys in place. A command with no keys has nothing to show and is left out.

props.name: level
props.description: Where the group headings stand in the outline: `3` by default - under the sheet's title, or a settings page's section.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, and the name of the command that opens it: in the palette and in the list itself.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: What the close button is called, for a screen reader. No default: a word the component invents is a word the product cannot translate.

props.name: description
props.description: The line under the heading.

props.name: keys
props.description: The keys that open it.

props.name: group
props.description: The heading its own line is listed under.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled, for a product that opens it from somewhere else as well.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the new state whenever it opens or closes, whether by the keys, `runCommand` or the close button.

props.name: children
props.description: After the list: what keys cannot say - a gesture with the pointer, a note that letters wait while someone is typing.

components.name: SkeletonOf
components.description: Shows the children, remembers their shape, and draws that shape back while the next load is in flight.

props.name: pending
props.description: Whether the content is on its way. While false the children are shown and measured; while true the remembered shape is drawn in their place.

props.name: children
props.description: The real thing. Rendered and measured when not pending.

props.name: rowSelector
props.description: What counts as a row - `'tr'`, `'li'`, `'[data-row]'`. Given, the placeholder draws one box per row at the height that row had; omitted, it draws a single box the height of the whole block.

props.name: fallback
props.description: What to draw before anything has been measured - the first load of a screen, where there is genuinely nothing to remember. A `SkeletonList` of roughly the right size is the usual answer.

props.name: shape
props.description: A shape measured earlier - from `measureShape`, stored by the product between sessions. Used until this instance measures something itself, so even a first load can be honest.

props.name: gapClassName
props.description: The gap between drawn rows, as a Tailwind class. Matches whatever the real list uses; the rows' own heights come from the measurement.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: One block. Size it with `className` - a skeleton is a shape, and the shape belongs to whatever it stands in for.

components.name: SkeletonText
components.description: A paragraph's worth of lines.

props.name: lines
props.description: How many lines of text stand here.

components.name: SkeletonList
components.description: Rows of a list, which is the shape most screens are waiting for.

props.name: rows
props.description: How many rows of the list stand here.

props.name: secondary
props.description: Draw a second, shorter line under each row - for a list whose rows carry a title and something beneath it.

components.name: SkeletonGrid
components.description: A grid of cells: a gallery, a board, a month.

props.name: cells
props.description: How many cells.

props.name: columns
props.description: How many per row.

props.name: cellClassName
props.description: The aspect of one cell, as a Tailwind class - a gallery of covers is not shaped like a grid of tiles.

props.name: value
props.description: A number for one thumb, an array for a range.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting value for an uncontrolled slider: a number, or an array for a range.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called on every change while the thumb moves, with a number or an array to match `value`.

props.name: onValueCommitted
props.description: Fires once when the drag ends, for the expensive thing a product does not want to run on every pixel of movement.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest value; Base UI's default is `0`.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest value; Base UI's default is `100`.

props.name: step
props.description: The increment a thumb moves by; Base UI's default is `1`.

props.name: minStepsBetweenValues
props.description: How close the thumbs of a range may come, in steps.

props.name: format
props.description: How the value reads when it is shown: `Intl.NumberFormat` options.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the track runs. A vertical slider is a fixed `h-40` tall.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the current value beside the track. Off by default: on a row of settings the numbers are noise, and where the figure matters a NumberField is the better control.

props.name: getThumbLabel
props.description: What each thumb is called, by index.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops the slider taking input.

props.name: name
props.description: The field name, for a form that posts the value.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the slider as a group, and is the fallback label of every thumb.

props.name: values
props.description: Oldest first. Fewer than two points is not a line, and draws nothing.

props.name: max
props.description: The top of the scale, so two lines can be compared by eye. Defaults to the highest value present, which makes the line self-scaled - fine for one line alone, wrong for a column of them.

props.name: label
props.description: What the line says, for a reader who cannot see it. Required: an unlabelled `img` is an unlabelled image, and this one carries information.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` sits beside a figure in a row, `md` beside a total. Defaults to `md`.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being waited for, for a screen reader. The product's word.

props.name: mark
props.description: The product's mark, drawn at 56px.

props.name: name
props.description: The product's name.

props.name: tagline
props.description: The line under the name.

props.name: version
props.description: The version, drawn in the mono face; the `v` is the product's to add.

props.name: status
props.description: What the application is doing right now.

props.name: tip
props.description: One thing worth knowing while it does it.

props.name: busy
props.description: Whether the bar is sweeping. Still and full when the application is waiting on something that has no progress, such as a person.

props.name: orientation
props.description: How the panes are laid out: `horizontal` is side by side, with upright handles between them; `vertical` stacks them.

props.name: defaultSizes
props.description: One percentage per pane, summing to 100 - what was saved from `onSizesChange`, or the product's opening layout. Equal shares without.

props.name: onSizesChange
props.description: Told the sizes when a change settles: persist them here.

props.name: step
props.description: Percent moved by an arrow key; Shift moves five of these.

props.name: min
props.description: Smallest size, 0 by default.

props.name: max
props.description: Largest size, 100 by default.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: Whether the pane can shrink past `min` to `collapsedSize`.

props.name: collapsedSize
props.description: Its size when collapsed: 0 by default, a rail's width for a pane that keeps its icons.

props.name: label
props.description: Names what the handle resizes: "Resize the sidebar". No default - it is the product's word.

props.name: tone
props.description: The reading tone. `default` and `accent` carry no judgement, so they need no mark.

props.name: icon
props.description: A glyph before the figure. Optional here.

props.name: label
props.description: What the figure is.

props.name: value
props.description: The figure. Already formatted - a duration, a count, a percentage: this component decides how a number looks, never what it says.

props.name: delta
props.description: Which way it moved, in words the caller chooses: `+12% vs last week`, `3 fewer than yesterday`. Omitted when there is nothing to compare to - an empty line here reads as "unchanged", which is a claim.

props.name: deltaTone
props.description: Whether that movement is good news. Stated rather than read off the sign, because for a figure like time-to-answer a fall is the good direction.

components.name: StatusDot
components.description: A dot, and the word it stands for.

props.name: label
props.description: What this condition is called, in the product's words. Required, and not for decoration: it is what the dot means to anyone who does not see the colour.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Whether to print the label beside the dot.

props.name: icon
props.description: A shape drawn inside the dot's place instead of the circle - a tick, a cross, an exclamation. The second channel for a reader who sees the dot but not its hue, and the reason `pulse` is not the only way to differ.

components.name: StatusBadge
components.description: The state, written out, on a tinted ground.

props.name: icon
props.description: A shape before the word - the second channel, where there is one.

props.name: dot
props.description: Draw the dot before the word. Off when an `icon` is given: two marks for one state is noise.

props.name: label
props.description: What the list is called for a reader - "Setup steps".

props.name: steps
props.description: The steps in the order they are taken. Each has an `id`, a `label` and an optional `description` and `status`.

props.name: current
props.description: The id of the step being shown.

props.name: stateLabels
props.description: The words for the states, read by a screen reader beside each label.

props.name: summary
props.description: The position in words - `(2, 5) => 'Step 2 of 5'`. Shown only when a horizontal stepper is too narrow for its labels. A function of the two numbers rather than a string, because the product says it in its own language and grammar.

props.name: onStepSelect
props.description: Makes reachable steps buttons. Without it the stepper is a picture of progress and nothing in it is a control.

props.name: reach
props.description: Which steps can be clicked. `visited` - the default - is done, failed and current ones; `any` also opens the ones ahead, which skips whatever check stands between here and there. Only a product that has made the steps independent should choose it.

props.name: orientation
props.description: A row across the top, or a column down the side. Only the row folds its labels away when narrow; a column has the height to keep them.

props.name: children
props.description: The words next to the switch. A switch with no label is a light with no caption - give `aria-label` if the meaning is genuinely in the context.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the switch is on, when the caller owns the state. Pair it with `onCheckedChange`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Whether the switch starts on, when it manages its own state.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Told the new state when the switch is flipped.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The switch cannot be flipped; it and its label dim.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the switch as required for a form.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The state shows but cannot be changed by the reader.

props.name: name
props.description: The field name submitted with a form.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the switch for a screen reader when it has no `children`.

components.name: TableScroll
components.description: The scroll container a table needs, and the one a sticky heading sticks in.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Keep the heading in view while the body scrolls under it.

props.name: selected
props.description: The row the reader has picked out - the one open in the panel beside the table, the one a keyboard cursor is on. Not a hover state.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Right-align and use the lining figures. For a column of numbers, and the reason it is a prop rather than a class the caller adds: a column of numbers that is not aligned is the most common defect in a table, and the one nobody files a bug about.

components.name: TableHeader
components.description: A plain heading, for a column that does not sort.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Right-align the heading, to sit over a `numeric` column of cells.

components.name: TableSortHeader
components.description: A heading that reorders the table when clicked.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Right-align the heading, to sit over a `numeric` column of cells.

props.name: column
props.description: This column's id - the key the accessor sorts by.

props.name: sort
props.description: What is sorted now, across the whole table.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called with this column's id when the heading is clicked. The product decides what comes next - the table does not sort or flip the direction.

props.name: colSpan
props.description: How many columns the message spans: the table's column count.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: A name for the list, when nothing on the screen already says what the tabs choose between. Documents in a window bar need one.

props.name: modified
props.description: The document has changes that are not saved.

props.name: modifiedLabel
props.description: What a reader hears for the dot, e.g. "unsaved changes".

props.name: onClose
props.description: Closes the tab: from the cross, a middle click, or Delete.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The cross's tooltip, e.g. "Close notes.md".

props.name: value
props.description: The tags. Controlled: the product owns the list.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the next list.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the text box, shown when there is room for it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the field. Required - a box of chips with no label names nothing.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Or points at a label element, when there is a visible one.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: How a tag's remove button is named, for a screen reader. Takes the tag, so the product can say "Remove documentation" in its own language.

props.name: max
props.description: Cap on how many tags may be added.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the field and stops it taking input or removing tags.

props.name: children
props.description: Drawn after the input, inside the box - a counter, a hint.

props.name: id
props.description: Put on the text box, so a `Field` label can point at it.

props.name: ref
props.description: A ref to the underlying `<textarea>` element, as a function or an object.

props.name: autoResize
props.description: Grow to fit the content instead of scrolling.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Stop growing here, in lines, and scroll instead.

components.name: TierBadge
components.description: The band, as a verdict.

props.name: status
props.type: accent | good | warn | bad | info | neutral

props.name: label
props.description: The band's name.

props.name: value
props.description: The number behind the verdict, if the product shows it. Drawn quieter than the name: the band is the answer and the score is the evidence.

components.name: TierRuler
components.description: The bands as a road, with the value standing somewhere along it.

props.name: tiers
props.description: The bands, in any order. Bands outside `min` to `max` are dropped.

props.name: value
props.description: Where the thing stands now.

props.name: min
props.description: The ends of the road.

props.name: max
props.description: The top end of the road; see `min`.

props.name: label
props.description: What the ruler as a whole is called, for a screen reader, and what to say the value is. The product's words - the ruler has none.

props.name: valueText
props.description: The value spoken instead of the bare number: "7.8 out of 10, publishable" is what a reader needs, and only the product can phrase it.

props.name: showLabels
props.description: Print the band names under the road.

components.name: AxisBar
components.description: One axis of a score, as a row of segments.

props.name: label
props.description: What this axis is called.

props.name: scale
props.description: The highest mark; one segment is drawn per whole point.

props.name: value
props.description: The mark, or `undefined` while the axis is unjudged. Not the same as zero: zero is a verdict, and a blank axis is the absence of one.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Given, the row becomes a control. Omitted, it is a read-only reading of a score someone else set.

props.name: threshold
props.description: The mark from which the total crosses into the next band, and what to call it. Absent when no mark on this axis gets there - and then nothing is drawn, because a line promising a band the axis cannot deliver is worse than no line.

props.name: valueText
props.description: What to say instead of the bare number - "unjudged", in the product's word, when there is no mark.

props.name: onPreview
props.description: The mark under the pointer, and `undefined` when the pointer leaves - so a product can say what a mark means while it is being weighed, before anyone commits to it. The question while scoring is about the mark being considered, not the one already given.

props.name: value
props.description: `HH:MM` in twenty-four hours, or `null` for empty.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Told the next time as `HH:MM`, or `null` when the box is cleared. Fires on blur and on Enter, not on every key, and not when the text parses to the time already held.

props.name: locale
props.description: How the time is shown while the field is not being typed into. The application's language unless stated - see `useLocale`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: What the empty box says. Pass the product's own words.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops the box taking focus or input. Passed to the `<input>`.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: The box can be focused and read but not typed into. Passed to the `<input>`.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the `<input>` as required for a form.

props.name: name
props.description: The `<input>`'s name, for a form.

props.name: id
props.description: The `<input>`'s id, so a label can point at it.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the `<input>`, for focusing it or reading its selection.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the box for a screen reader when no visible label does.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The id of the element that describes the box, such as a hint.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: The list itself.

props.name: side
props.description: Draw the rail and the markers on the right of the text, for a right-to-left reading or a history beside a wider body of content.

components.name: TimelineItem
components.description: One entry: a marker, a rail down to the next, and what happened.

props.name: status
props.type: accent | good | warn | bad | info | neutral

props.name: pending
props.description: A step not taken yet: the ring of a dot with nothing in it, which is how every other tool draws "not done" and is worth borrowing. Its glyph is `dim`, whatever the status: the fill it was paired with is not there to read it against.

props.name: title
props.description: The headline of the entry - what happened.

props.name: time
props.description: When it happened. Drawn quieter, and given as a node so the product can pass its own `RelativeTime` rather than a string it formatted early.

props.name: icon
props.description: A shape inside the marker - a tick, a cross, a number. The second channel, for a reader who does not separate the hues.

props.name: last
props.description: The last entry does not draw a rail below it. Set by the product, because only it knows whether the history ends here or merely stops being shown.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: Names the state in the product's words, for a reader who does not see the colour. Required whenever `status` carries meaning the title does not already say.

components.name: ToastProvider
components.description: Wraps the part of the application that can raise a toast. One per screen; nesting them gives a product two queues that do not know about each other.

components.name: ToastTitle
components.description: The heading. Base UI points the toast's `aria-labelledby` at it.

components.name: ToastDescription
components.description: The sentence under it, and the toast's `aria-describedby`. The part that scrolls when the sentence is longer than the window.

components.name: ToastAction
components.description: The one thing the reader can do about it: undo, or go and look.

components.name: ToastClose
components.description: The dismiss button. Needs a word - a bare cross is announced as nothing.

components.name: Toast
components.description: One toast. The tone comes from the caller or from `toast.type`, so a product that raises them through the manager gets the stripe for free.

components.name: ToastViewport
components.description: Where they stack. Bottom right by default, which is the corner that does not cover a form being filled in or a menu being read.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the document body, which is what keeps toasts above everything regardless of where they were raised from.

components.name: TooltipProvider
components.description: A shared delay for a group of tooltips. Wrap a toolbar in it and the second icon button explains itself instantly rather than making the reader wait again. Optional - a lone tooltip works without one.

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: The root. Takes `disabled`, and the controlled `open`/`onOpenChange`.

components.name: TooltipTrigger
components.description: What it labels. Give it `render` to use your own button - and give that button an `aria-label` saying what the tooltip says, because the tooltip itself reaches nobody using a screen reader.

components.name: TooltipPopup
components.description: The label itself. Portalled and positioned, so it is not clipped by an ancestor with `overflow: hidden`.

props.name: side
props.type: bottom | top | left | right | inline-end | inline-start
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger. Base UI flips it when it does not fit, and defaults it to the top.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment along that side. Base UI centres it by default.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Distance from the trigger, in pixels.

props.name: arrow
props.description: Whether to draw the arrow pointing back at the trigger.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null
props.description: Where to portal to. Defaults to the raised host of the overlay this is opened inside (`layer.tsx`), and to the document body when there is none - either way not the element it was opened from, whose `overflow` would clip it. Pass an element to put it somewhere else, such as a container being screenshotted.

components.name: TooltipArrow
components.description: The notch pointing back at the trigger. Base UI rotates it to whatever side the tooltip landed on, which is why the placement is keyed off `data-side` rather than off the `side` that was asked for.

props.name: segments
props.description: The stretches to draw: each has a `key`, a `start` and an `end`, and optionally a `tone` and a `label`.

props.name: from
props.description: The value the left edge stands for. Defaults to the earliest segment.

props.name: to
props.description: The value the right edge stands for. Defaults to the latest segment.

props.name: marker
props.description: Where the position marker stands, on the same scale as the segments. Omitted when there is no such thing - a day of work has no "you are here".

props.name: label
props.description: What the whole bar says, for a reader who cannot see it. Required: the segments are decoration to a screen reader, and their titles are not announced in order.

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Override the floor under a segment's width - `0` draws everything exactly to scale.

props.name: divided
props.description: Separate adjacent segments with a hairline of the ground.

props.name: nodes
props.description: The tree, as nested nodes. Only the folders in `open` show their children.

props.name: open
props.description: Which folders are open. Uncontrolled if omitted.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Told the new set of open folders whenever one opens or shuts, whether the tree is controlled or not.

props.name: selected
props.description: Which row is chosen - the file being edited, not the one the cursor is on. The two move apart: a reader walks the tree with arrows without opening anything until Enter.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the id of a leaf when it is chosen by click, Enter or Space. A folder toggles instead.

props.name: label
props.description: What a screen reader calls the tree. Required: a bare tree announces "tree" and nothing else, and the word belongs to the product.

props.name: children
props.description: The text. A string, because the component has to be able to put it in a `title` - arbitrary children could not be.

props.name: lines
props.description: Cut after this many lines. One by default.

props.name: title
props.description: Say what the full text is on hover. On by default; turn it off where the text is already visible elsewhere, or the tooltip is noise.

props.name: rows
props.description: Every row there is, in order. Only the ones in view are drawn.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: How tall one row is. Fixed, and the component enforces it - a row that grows past this height overlaps its neighbour, which is why the value is required rather than measured.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: A stable identity per row. Without it React keys by index, and a list that is sorted or filtered reuses the wrong DOM node - the row moves but its input keeps the text that was typed into a different row.

props.name: overscan
props.description: How many extra rows to draw beyond each edge, so a fast scroll does not paint blank.

props.name: label
props.description: What a screen reader calls the list. Required: a scrolling box of rows with no name is announced as "list" and nothing else, and the word is the product's to give.

components.name: WindowButtons
components.description: The window controls, in the order Windows puts them.

props.name: labels
props.type: { minimize: string; maximize: string; restore: string; close: string; }
props.description: What each button is called. Required, and deliberately without a default: a string this component invents is a string the product cannot translate. `restore` replaces `maximize` while the window is maximised.

components.name: ResizeEdges
components.description: Invisible strips along the window's edges.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged into every strip. `fixed` to the viewport by default, which is where a window's edges are; `absolute` puts them on the nearest positioned box instead, for a frame drawn inside a page.

components.name: TitleBar
components.description: A frameless window's title bar, assembled.

props.name: labels
props.type: { minimize: string; maximize: string; restore: string; close: string; }
props.description: The window buttons' names; see `WindowButtons`.

props.name: mark
props.description: The product's mark, at the left edge, where the system put the icon.

props.name: children
props.description: What the window shows at the top: its open documents as `<Tabs><TabsList variant="bar">`, a trail, or a title.

props.name: actions
props.description: The product's own controls, between the handle and the window buttons.

props.name: center
props.description: Something that belongs to the whole window rather than to either end - the search box, most often - held at the window's centre.

props.name: steps
props.description: The steps, in order. Each has an `id`, a label, its `content`, and optional checks that run before the wizard moves on.

props.name: step
props.description: The step shown, for a controlled wizard.

props.name: defaultStep
props.description: The step shown first, for an uncontrolled one. The first step if omitted.

props.name: onStepChange
props.description: Called with the step to move to - after its checks have passed, when moving forward. A controlled wizard moves when the product sets `step`.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Called when Finish is pressed on the last step and its checks pass.

props.name: onError
props.description: Called when a step's `onNext` throws. The step is blocked and marked failed either way; without this the error is rethrown so it is not lost.

props.name: stepperLabel
props.description: The stepper's name for a reader.

props.name: stateLabels
props.description: The words for a step's state - done, failed, and optionally not yet reached - which the stepper says to a screen reader beside the mark.

props.name: summary
props.description: The position in words, such as `(2, 5) => 'Step 2 of 5'`. The stepper shows it when it is too narrow for its labels.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: The buttons' words. Required: the component has none of its own.

props.name: nextLabel
props.description: The words of the button that goes to the next step.

props.name: finishLabel
props.description: The words of the button on the last step that finishes the wizard.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Stepper above the content, or beside it.

props.name: level
props.description: Where a step's title stands in the page's outline: `2` by default, under the screen's title.

props.name: title
props.description: "Welcome to kilna".

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the title that says what the dashboard is for.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons at the end of the header - the product's own, such as "Import data".

props.name: steps
props.description: The first steps, in order. Each is marked done or not, and only the first one not yet done carries its `action`.

props.name: figures
props.description: The figures the full dashboard will have. Leave it out to show only the steps.

props.name: words
props.description: Every word the screen shows, in the product's language. The block has no default text.

props.name: title
props.description: The screen's title.

props.name: description
props.description: One sentence under it.

props.name: actions
props.description: What acts on the screen as a whole: New, Import.

props.name: items
props.description: What the list holds, in the order it shows.

props.name: itemKey
props.description: A stable key per item: its id.

props.name: row
props.description: How an item reads as a row.

props.name: selected
props.description: The key of what is open, or null.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Told what to open - or null, to go back to the list.

props.name: matches
props.description: Whether an item answers to what was typed. Leave it out and there is no search: a list of seven does not need one.

props.name: detailTitle
props.description: The open item's title: the heading of its pane and the name of the region that scrolls. Words, because a region is named in words.

props.name: detailActions
props.description: What acts on the open item, beside its title.

props.name: detail
props.description: The open item itself.

props.name: emptyAction
props.description: The one thing worth doing on an empty screen: "New work".

props.name: rowRender
props.description: A row drawn as something other than a button - the product's link, so a row can be opened in a new tab: `(work) => <Link to={…} />`. A click is then the link's: the router opens it and `selected` follows the address. `onSelect` is still told by the keyboard and the way back.

props.name: words
props.description: Every word the screen shows: the list's name, the search box, the way back, and what each empty state says. Words are passed in so the product can translate them.

props.name: title
props.description: "Sign in to kilna".

props.name: description
props.description: A line under it, when the title does not say enough.

props.name: mark
props.description: The product's mark, above the title: `<ProductMark product="kilna" size={40} />`.

props.name: identifier
props.description: What the first field asks for. An email gets the keyboard and the check a browser gives an address; a user name gets neither.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Resolve with nothing when signed in; with words when refused - "That email and password do not match." Reject when there was no answer.

props.name: extra
props.description: Under the password: "Forgot your password?"

props.name: footer
props.description: Under the panel: "No account? Ask whoever runs this server."

props.name: words
props.description: Every string the screen shows: the two field labels, the show and hide names of the password toggle, the submit button in both states, and the message for a server that could not be reached. The block has no words of its own.

props.name: title
props.description: The screen's title.

props.name: description
props.description: One sentence under the title.

props.name: sections
props.description: The sections, in the order the column lists them.

props.name: active
props.description: The open section's id. Null opens the column on a narrow screen and the first section where there is room for both.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Told which section to open - or null, to go back to the column.

props.name: sectionRender
props.description: A section drawn as the product's link, so it has an address: `(section) => <Link to={`/settings/${section.id}`} />`. A press is then the link's; `onSelect` is still told on the way back.

props.name: words
props.description: The column's name and the way back, in the product's language.

components.name: SettingsGroup
components.description: A group of settings inside a section.

props.name: title
props.description: The group's caption: "Appearance", "Notifications".

props.name: description
props.description: A line under it, when the caption does not say enough.

props.name: children
props.description: Its fields, one under another.
